A diversion is the largest disturbance to sector throughput and is not needed when dest_disruption=6 is low.

ranking.rationale: Earlier slot keeps the stream regular and avoids adding taxi or airborne time; dest_disruption=6 is low against nominal_aar=126 (assumed), so no peak pressure requires a later slot.
Small earlier shift disturbs the arrival stream least and adds nothing to taxiways at the peak.
Holding at origin keeps the aircraft off the congested destination taxiways and out of the airborne stream.
Small later shift keeps the stream regular, though it does not add value on final given low dest_disruption.
Larger later shift is acceptable for spacing but moves the arrival further from the planned stream.
Adds 2 min of taxi at destination during congestion, a modest cost to taxiway flow.
Adds 5 min of taxi at destination during congestion, which is worse for taxiway flow than GATE_A12.
Airborne hold adds traffic into the sector stream and wake-separated final approach, which is undesirable when a slot shift is available.
Longer airborne hold disturbs the arrival stream more and adds airborne traffic into final approach.
Diversion removes the flight from our runway sequence entirely, the largest sector disturbance; no ATC need justifies it.
Diversion with the longest estimated delay disturbs the sector most; no ATC need justifies it.

vetoes.reason: Forty minutes of airborne holding in weather draws on an estimated fuel reserve and is the most exposed place to be.

ranking.rationale: Holding on the ground at origin adds no airborne time against the estimated fuel reserve and avoids weather exposure.
Earlier slot adds no airborne hold and keeps the duty day shorter, with no knock-on delay estimated.
Earlier slot with no airborne time protects fuel, though the magnitude relies on the estimated slot figure.
Only 2 minutes extra taxi, negligible fuel draw and no airborne time.
Five minutes extra taxi is a small fuel and duty cost, acceptable but worse than A12.
Adds 15 minutes delay that the crew would prefer to avoid; the connection is still reachable at the destination.
Thirty minutes later erodes duty time and the connection margin; tolerable only if nothing better is available.
Airborne hold draws on the estimated fuel reserve and is exposed to weather at destination.
Forty-minute hold near destination in weather draws heavily on an estimated fuel reserve; refused.
Diversion adds a second approach and loses the connection, though it avoids the weather; last resort.
Longest diversion adds the most airborne time and loses the connection; least preferred.
Earlier arrival keeps the gate plan closest to schedule with zero est_knock_on_min; gate fit against the synthetic occupancy is only partly checkable.
Gate swap is a tool we own; est_delay_min is small and est_knock_on_min is 0, though the gate model is synthetic and turnaround_source is assumed.
Larger earlier shift, knock-on 0, but feasibility of an earlier arrival against gate occupancy is uncertain on synthetic data.
Modest delay with knock-on 0 and the assigned gate A6 free before the listed A6 occupancy window.
Adds ramp arrival delay but knock-on is 0; acceptable while ramp congestion is moderate.
Larger extra taxi than A12 and est_delay_min is higher, but knock-on is still 0.
Longer delay pushes arrival later; knock-on 0 but turnaround delay for the tail grows.
Longest acceptable hold; adds meaningful turnaround delay with no downstream legs to offset it.
Delay is at BOS, not our hub; provides no gate benefit at ATL, so low ground value.
Diversion removes the aircraft from our gate plan and adds about 80 minutes; downstream_legs is empty so harshness is reduced, but it is not preferred.
Diversion removes the aircraft from our gate plan and adds the longest delay on the menu; not preferred.

vetoes.reason: Diversion takes the flight off the destination runway and disturbs the arrival stream most; the destination is disrupted but still the arrival point.
Diversion takes the flight off the destination runway and disturbs the arrival stream most; the destination is disrupted but still the arrival point.

ranking.rationale: Moves the arrival away from the destination peak and keeps aircraft off taxiways; dest_disruption is high for this hour (data).
Earlier slot moves the arrival off the disrupted peak with a small disturbance to the stream.
Holding at origin keeps aircraft off the congested taxiways and adds no airborne holding into final.
Later slot avoids airborne holding but places the arrival into the disrupted hour, so wake spacing on final is less favourable.
Larger later shift places the arrival into the disrupted hour; acceptable only as a fallback.
Adds a little taxi time in a congested taxiway environment, with minimal stream disturbance.
Longer taxi route adds more aircraft time on congested taxiways than GATE_A12.
Airborne hold adds traffic into the disrupted final approach; disturbs the arrival stream.
Longest airborne hold feeds the most traffic into the disrupted peak; accepted only as a concession to the GROUND position.
Diversion removes the arrival from the destination runway and disturbs the arrival stream most.
Diversion removes the arrival from the destination runway and disturbs the arrival stream most.

vetoes.reason: 40 minutes of airborne hold draws on estimated fuel reserve and is the most exposed place in weather.

ranking.rationale: Earliest arrival option with no airborne time, so it draws nothing on fuel_reserve_min=103.8 (estimated) and protects the connection.
Earlier arrival with no holding, preserving fuel and duty time; estimated reserve is a reason to avoid airborne delay.
Delay taken on the ground at origin, so no airborne fuel burn and no weather exposure; accepted as tolerable.
Small delay with no holding; acceptable but adds time against crew_duty_remaining_min=103.

Keeping veto: 40 minutes of airborne hold draws on estimated fuel_reserve_min=103.8 and holding in weather is the most exposed option.
Diversion adds a second approach and loses the ABQ connection; ranked below destination arrival.
Longer diversion than CSG, adds a second approach and loses the connection; ranked below destination arrival.
Earlier slot keeps the arrival nearest the scheduled gate window with zero knock-on; gate model is synthetic and turnaround_source is assumed.
Larger earlier shift also has zero knock-on, but moves further from the planned arrival; acceptable if the earlier slot is available.
Keeps the aircraft landing on time with only a 2-minute extra taxi; zero knock-on at the current ramp level.
Modest later arrival with zero knock-on, but adds a 15-minute delay to the turnaround window.
